approval.decisions: OQ-23: 325 slot minimums in 21 groups; 70 conditioning, power and mobility entries; counting rules; seed baseline 67/325 and 20/70 accepted
approval.statement: The coverage framework is an acceptance mechanism, not a demand to populate exercises to satisfy numbers. Quality and meaningful variation take precedence.

description: Machine-readable slot inventory behind coverage-matrix.md (approved 2026-11-05). The framework is an acceptance mechanism, not a demand to populate exercises to satisfy numbers; quality and meaningful variation take precedence. Every number is derived from the enumerated entries: a slot minimum is the number of counted entries; a group minimum is the sum of its slot minimums; mechanics, laterality and equipment-class minimums are the counts of those values among the counted entries. Entries marked counted:false are optional and legitimate but never a minimum. Entry names are intended exercises, not required names: CI counts catalogue exercises by the slot rules below, not by name. Minimums are measurable from catalogue data alone.

countingRules.group: An exercise counts toward a group when one of its PRIMARY targets is a node listed in the group nodes or a descendant, AND its primary pattern (first pattern) is one of the patterns of at least one slot of that group. Secondary targets never count. fullBody never counts. Only exercises of category push, pull, legs or core count toward an anatomical group (revision 3, N6); fullBody, cardio and mobility exercises are measured in the conditioning, power and mobility sets (tranche 5.7). Retired, user and imported exercises never count.
countingRules.slot: An exercise fills at most ONE slot per group. A slot accepts an exercise when the group rule holds, the primary pattern is one of the slot patterns, and every discriminator term holds. Assignment of exercises to slots is a deterministic maximum bipartite matching (ties broken by exercise id); slots are met when the matching fills slot.min of them.

discriminatorKinds.attribute: recorded optional controlled exercise attribute equals one of values (an unrecorded attribute never matches)
discriminatorKinds.mechanics: mechanics is in values (unset never matches)
discriminatorKinds.subTarget: the exercise has the node or a descendant as a target; role primary or any

countingRules.noL4Primary: No slot or minimum depends on an L4 primary tag (F03). L4 tagging stays optional. A discriminator of kind subTarget names an L2 or L3 node only.
countingRules.dimensions: Compound, isolation, bilateral, unilateral-or-alternating and equipment-class minimums are counted over the exercises that fill slots (not over all exercises of the group).
countingRules.variationFamilies: Minimum number of variationOf families in the group with a root and at least three variations. Derived: the number of slots with at least four counted entries. There is no cap on family size.

caps.family: No family cap (revision 3, N1). A cap on the share of one variationOf family contradicts the variation rules (a flat bench press family can legitimately hold 18 variations, a biceps curl group is one family of 17). Diversity is enforced by the slots themselves: each slot names a distinct function, class or position and has its own minimum. The minimum number of families remains (variationFamilies).
caps.equipmentClass: At most max(55 percent of the group total, 4 exercises) in one equipment class; the bodyweight class is exempt in groups with bodyweightExempt true (abs, obliques, lowerBack). The inventory itself satisfies this cap by construction (checked by the validation script).

exerciseAttributesProposed.status: Approved 2026-11-05. Optional controlled attributes of an exercise, used only as slot discriminators and by the duplicate checks. ADR-0008 implication: ADR-0008 has no attribute store (generic attribute stores were rejected as option 3 for classifications); each attribute would be an optional single-valued column or one small child table with a controlled value list, i.e. an amendment or clarification of ADR-0008 and a change to the release format. Amended 2026-11-06: the owner signed off X1. The angle, armPosition and kneePosition texts now equal the code.
exerciseAttributesProposed.ifDeclined: NOT USED. The owner approved the seven attributes with their vocabulary and boundary rules on 2026-11-05. The pattern-level fallback in attributeFallback is retained only as a record of the measurable alternative.

angle.definition: Angle of the bench or the body to the horizontal in a press or fly.

values.flat: Bench or body from 10 degrees head-down to 10 degrees head-up inclusive.
values.incline: Bench raised more than 10 and up to 45 degrees (steeper is a vertical push, rule R2).
values.decline: Bench lowered with the head more than 10 and up to 90 degrees below the hips.

armPosition.definition: Position of the working upper arm relative to the trunk at the start of the movement.

values.besideBody: Upper arm hangs by the side, from 0 to 20 degrees inclusive from the trunk line, in any direction.
values.behindBody: Elbow behind the trunk line by more than 20 and up to 180 degrees (for example an incline curl). Takes precedence over overhead.
values.supportedInFront: Upper arm rests on a pad, bench or thigh in front of the trunk, at any angle from 0 to 180 degrees from the trunk line. Takes precedence over every other arm value.
values.overhead: Upper arm raised forward or to the side more than 135 and up to 180 degrees from the trunk line (typically with the elbow at or above ear height). Not used for an arm behind the trunk.
values.flexed90: Upper arm raised forward more than 20 and up to 135 degrees from the trunk line (typically about 90 degrees).
values.abducted90: Upper arm raised to the side more than 20 and up to 135 degrees from the trunk line (typically 90/90 with the elbow bent).

bodyPosition.definition: Position of the trunk and the support while the exercise is performed.

values.lying: On the back or side, supported along the length of the trunk.
values.prone: Face down, trunk supported on a bench or the floor.
values.bentOver: Standing with the hips hinged forward and the trunk unsupported.
values.kneeling: On both knees or on all fours.
values.halfKneeling: One knee down, one foot forward.
values.inclined: Back or chest supported on an inclined surface, or the upper back on a bench with the hips free (hip thrust).

grip.definition: Hand orientation on the handle or bar.

values.supinated: Palms facing up or towards the face.

gripWidth.definition: Distance between the hands relative to the shoulders.

values.wide: Hands outside shoulder width by more than a hand width.

kneePosition.definition: Knee angle during a calf or lower-leg movement.

values.straight: Knee from fully straight (0 degrees) to 10 degrees of flexion inclusive.
values.bent: Knee bent more than 10 and up to 180 degrees of flexion (typically about 90).

stance.definition: Foot placement relative to the hips.

values.split: One foot ahead of the other.

primariesPerExercise.description: Per tranche, over the new system exercises of the tranche.
primariesPerExercise.threeOrMorePrimaries: allowed only with a reviewer note
primariesPerExercise.status: Approved thresholds; re-baselined after the pilot.

groupWithTotalBelow20.advanced: optional; record the reason if none

pilot.statement: Tranche 5.1 (chest) is the PILOT. After 5.1 a mandatory re-baselining step runs: the slot inventory, thresholds (duplicate score, caps, primaries per exercise) and difficulty bands are re-derived from what the pilot showed, and tranches 5.2 to 5.7 start only after the owner explicitly approves the revised coverage.json.

groups.label: Chest
groups.basis: Pectoralis major has clavicular and sternocostal fibres, so presses at three angles and flys are needed; serratus anterior and pectoralis minor move the shoulder blade and need protraction work. Presses are discriminated by recorded angle, never by an L4 primary tag.

slots.label: Flys with free weights or bodyweight
Shoulder blade protraction (serratus anterior, pectoralis minor)

groups.label: Upper back
groups.basis: The trapezius works in three parts (elevation, retraction, depression) and the rhomboids retract. Rows load retraction, shrugs elevation, low-angle work the lower trapezius. Which row exercises carry an upper-back primary depends on the primary-muscle principle (resolved at tranche review); the row slots count whichever exercises the owner decision tags with an upper-back primary.

slots.label: Rows with free weights, Smith machine or kettlebell

groups.label: Lats
groups.basis: The latissimus dorsi extends and adducts the arm. Vertical pulls load it through the full range, close-grip rows in a shorter range, and straight-arm work isolates shoulder extension.

slots.label: Pulldowns and assisted pull-ups on machines and cables
Lat-emphasis rows with free weights or a kettlebell
Lat-emphasis rows on cables and machines

groups.label: Shoulders (deltoid)
groups.basis: The deltoid has three heads with different jobs: front (flexion, pressing), side (abduction), rear (extension, horizontal abduction). Each needs its own slot. Superficial variants (seat angle, hand rotation of a few degrees, tempo) are not enumerated: lateral and rear-delt slots list only entries that change the implement, the line of pull or the side worked.

slots.label: Overhead presses on machine, Smith machine or cable
Rear-delt work on machines and cables
Rear-delt work with free weights, bands or bodyweight

groups.label: Rotator cuff
groups.basis: The four cuff muscles rotate and centre the humerus. Work is low load and single-joint: external rotation (infraspinatus, teres minor), internal rotation (subscapularis) and abduction (supraspinatus). No machine, Smith machine or kettlebell exercise is forced (F07).

slots.label: External rotation, arm at the side

groups.label: Neck
groups.basis: Neck flexors, extensors, side flexors and rotators each need one low-load isolation pattern. Safety wording must be conservative. The neck is included by owner decision (2026-11-05): conventional gym exercises only; no machine or cable entry is forced (F07).

groups.label: Biceps and brachialis
groups.basis: The elbow flexors bend the elbow in different forearm positions: biceps (supinated), brachialis (any), brachioradialis (neutral and pronated; counted under Forearms). Slots are discriminated by the recorded arm position or grip, which is how the long and short biceps heads are covered without an L4 minimum. Only entries that change the arm position, grip, implement or side worked are listed (superficial-variant risk, F07).

slots.label: Curls with the arm beside the body
Curls with the arm behind the body
Curls with the arm supported in front

groups.label: Triceps
groups.basis: The triceps extend the elbow; the long head also crosses the shoulder, so overhead and neutral-arm positions load it differently. Overhead work is the discriminator for the long head ("at least n exercises with the arm overhead").

slots.label: Pushdowns with the arm beside the body

groups.label: Forearms and grip
groups.basis: Flexors and extensors of wrist and fingers, pronators and supinators, and brachioradialis. Grip holds use the finger flexors. Brachioradialis work is counted here, not under Biceps and brachialis.

groups.label: Glutes
groups.basis: Gluteus maximus extends the hip; medius and minimus abduct and stabilise the pelvis. Hip extension slots are split by recorded body position (lying or inclined, kneeling or standing, prone), class and laterality, so that a bridge, a kickback and a reverse hyperextension each have their own slot (a single exercise fills one slot only). Hinge slots count exercises with a glutes primary; deadlift primaries depend on the primary-muscle principle at tranche review.

slots.label: Reverse and hip-driven extensions (prone; decision rule R5)
Lunges and steps with a glutes primary
Gluteus medius stability and abduction (bodyweight, side-lying, band)

groups.label: Abductors
groups.basis: Open-chain hip abduction against external resistance (machine, cable, standing band): primary abductors with gluteusMedius as secondary. Bodyweight and stability drills belong to the gluteusMedius slot of Glutes (functional double tag, editorial guide 5.7). No Smith machine or kettlebell entry exists.

groups.label: Adductors
groups.basis: Hip adduction with the adductor muscles. Wide-stance compound lifts count only if tagged primary and their primary pattern is a slot pattern of this group (they are not).

groups.label: Hip flexors
groups.basis: Iliopsoas lifts the thigh. Standing drives, cable and band work and supine marches give coverage. Hanging and lying leg raises with an abdominal primary count under Abs.

groups.label: Deep hip rotators
groups.basis: Small rotators behind the hip; light, controlled work. No cable entry is forced (F07).

groups.label: Quadriceps
groups.basis: Four heads extend the knee; squats, lunges and extensions load them through different ranges. Rectus femoris also flexes the hip. Squat and lunge slots are split by implement class because the load path differs. No cable entry is forced (F07). The trap bar deadlift has a hinge primary pattern and so counts toward no quadriceps slot.

slots.label: Lunges and steps with free weights
Bodyweight lunges, steps and single-leg squats

groups.label: Hamstrings
groups.basis: Hamstrings extend the hip and flex the knee. Hinges load the hip function; curls load the knee function. Knee-flexion variants differ by body position (seated, lying, standing, supported) and support, which gives fewer legitimate entries than elbow flexion (arm position and grip); the smaller figure is deliberate and reviewable (F07).

groups.label: Calves
groups.basis: Gastrocnemius works best with a straight knee; soleus with a bent knee. The recorded knee position discriminates the two slots, so there is no L4 or L3 primary minimum.

slots.label: Calf raises with a straight knee

entries.name: Bodyweight calf raise on a step

slots.label: Calf raises with a bent knee

groups.label: Shin and outer lower leg
groups.basis: Tibialis anterior, the fibularis muscles and tibialis posterior support the ankle. Light, single-joint work.

groups.label: Abs
groups.basis: Rectus abdominis flexes the trunk and resists extension; transversus abdominis braces. Bodyweight work is legitimate and common, so the bodyweight class is exempt from the class cap in this group.

slots.label: Leg and knee raises with an abdominal primary

groups.label: Obliques
groups.basis: Obliques rotate, side-flex and resist rotation and side flexion. Unilateral and alternating work is the norm; bodyweight is exempt from the class cap.

groups.label: Lower back
groups.basis: Erector spinae extend and brace the spine; quadratus lumborum resists side flexion; multifidus stiffens the spine. Classified by the joint that moves (rule R5): only exercises in which the spine itself moves into extension, or holds against it, have a lower-back primary and the pattern trunkExtension. Back extensions done with a neutral spine and the hips as the hinge, reverse hyperextensions and good mornings are hip-dominant: their primaries are glutes or hamstrings as the tranche review settles under the primary-muscle principle, with lowerBack as a secondary, and they count in those groups. The lower-back minimum is therefore small and honest (revision 3).

slots.label: Hinges with a lower-back primary (primary depends on the primary-muscle principle at tranche review; optional only)

sets.label: Ergometer work
sets.note: Ski ergometer and stair climber need the proposed equipment items.

sets.label: Ballistic hinge (category fullBody)
sets.note: Counts only exercises of category fullBody, so that deadlifts are not counted here.

sets.label: Whole-body conditioning
sets.note: Battle rope wave needs the proposed battleRopes item.

sets.label: Static stretches, one per coverage group
Soft tissue release (deferred by owner decision; optional)
sets.note: All entries optional. Soft tissue release content is deferred by owner decision (2026-11-05); the count is 0.
